newsitem.title: UK: LucasVarity powers ahead on outlook.
newsitem.headline: LucasVarity powers ahead on outlook.

text.p: LucasVarity Plc, the recently merged Anglo-U.S. engineering group, saw its shares power ahead on Tuesday after announcing that forecasts of 280 million pounds ($451.7 million) pre-tax profit for the year were "realistic".
The auto components to aerospace group also noted that it was "optimistic that overall growth can be achieved in 1997".
LucasVarity promised not to cut dividends without launching a share buyback, news that helped to send its shares jumping 13.5 pence higher to 219 pence by the 1630 GMT close.
"The board would not consider a reduction in the dividend without announcing a share repurchase programme," the company said in a statement.
Analysts said Victor Rice, the chief executive, told them later in a telephone conference call that he was in favour of buybacks but failed to be drawn further.
In the meantime the dividend is expected to be maintained.
"The intention of LucasVarity's board of directors is to declare a dividend of 2.1 pence related to the short period ended January 31," said the company statement.

The dividend news was the main support for the share price, one analyst said. In recent weeks, the shares had been weighed down by concerns of a possible dividend suspension after LucasVarity reported tough trading conditions in early December.
Some investors had interpreted this as a profit warning, leading shares to tumble by 17 percent until a very recent comeback, assisted by a repeated buy recommendation from brokers SocGen.

Commenting on gearing, the group said it should be in the 70 percent-plus range for the year to January 31, but that this level would drop quickly thereafter. Analysts were told gearing could be around the 30 percent mark by 1998.
In a divisional breakdown, the group said that the French car market was weak but that North America and Europe had held up well in the latter part of the year.
But heavy duty vehicles were suffering with the North American market down 25 percent and Europe 11 percent weaker.
Diesel engines remained sluggish but aerospace was enjoying a healthy order book and "the outlook remains positive for commercial airframe deliveries", it noted. ($1=.6199 Pound)
